summary.title: 85 Things I learned being a CEO
summary.one_liner: A founder-CEO's list of 85 lessons on decision making, culture, leadership, hiring, fundraising and self-management in a startup.
takeaways: Run one-on-ones at least monthly and set quarterly goals; give feedback based on facts and include a path to improve.
Decide quickly, accept and explain mistakes, and treat culture as something to repeatedly speak about and protect.
Hire for culture fit and role-specific objective evaluation; use Yes/Weak Yes/No interview verdicts with a single No blocking a hire.
Attend only meetings where you decide or receive needed information, and prepare about 30 minutes per hour of meeting you chair.
Raise money in good times, choose investors you can work with, and track monthly cash outflow, revenue, salaries and bank balance.
summary.summary: This is a long, opinion-based list of lessons from a startup CEO, written as short bullet points grouped into sections: key responsibilities, decision making, culture, leadership, self-management, people management and HR, meetings, hiring, fundraising, and personal habits. Each point is a direct piece of advice rather than a tutorial, and several cite Andy Grove's book High Output Management for one-on-ones and running meetings. The author gives concrete rules of thumb, such as hiring an HR person around 30 employees, introducing formal performance management at 40-50 employees, and a monthly All Hands meeting. The page is anecdotal and contains no code or data beyond the author's own experience.
